segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And the Caliph endured until it came out.
And he commanded Salim, the chief of the eunuchs,
to choose three Byzantine maidservants who were exceptionally beautiful,
and take them to the physician's house along with three thousand dinars.
And he did so.
And when he brought them,
George was not present at home.
And when he arrived and saw them,
he was angry with his disciple,
and said to him:
"O disciple of Satan,
why did you bring these in to me? Do you want to lead me into old-age sin?" And he sent and called the eunuch,
and sent them back with him.
And when the Caliph heard this, he said to him:
"Why did you send the maidservants back?" And he replied:
"May you live forever!
We Christians are not allowed more than one wife,
and as long as the wife of one of us is alive,
our law forbids taking another."
And this pleased the Caliph greatly,
and he ordered that he might enter without hindrance {OCR?} to his wives and his daughters.
And his honor increased with him,
and he loved him as his own soul.
For such is the fruit of chastity,
my brethren.
After Abu Ja'far, al-Mahdi, his son, [ruled for] ten years.
He opened his father's treasuries,
and scattered his father's wealth as if with a winnowing shovel,
not only upon his armies,
but also upon the women of his harems {OCR?},
because he was wanton and a lover of pleasures.
And he was inclined after horoscopes, divinations, and omens,
and he collected books of sorcery.
Therefore King Leo sent him the book of Jannes and Jambres,
which contains all the sorcery of the Egyptians,
and everything that they did against the great Moses.
And at the beginning of his reign he freed all the Christian captives,
and Leo likewise freed the Arab captives who were with him.
Then al-Mahdi demolished the churches that had been built in the time of the Arabs,
and the church of the Chalcedonians in Aleppo was ruined.
And he raised a persecution against the Manichaeans,
and the place called Paddana the Great was uprooted,
which was entirely full of Manichaeans.
And many Arabs were caught in this heresy and were killed.
And also from the family of Gummaya eight honorable men were seized unjustly,
and after many afflictions,
three died in prison,
and five were saved.
At this time, Theophilus, son of Thomas of Edessa, became known,
a man who was an astronomer
